long_biography.plain_text:
Aviation executive Keren McLendon cites a payroll correction as an enduring lesson from company founder Sidney Robinson. When a benefits calculation left some employees underpaid and others overpaid, Robinson paid the shortfalls without reclaiming the excess. McLendon has described that decision as a model for her own management.

She began her career in accounting without intending to enter aviation. In encouraging other women to advance in the industry, she stresses asking colleagues for help and building professional relationships. She also serves on the board of the Oklahoma City chapter of Women in Aviation, which promotes opportunities in the field.
